articleTitle: Harmonic considerations on low voltage systems
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1991 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: Guidelines are developed for applying capacitors and harmonic-producing loads on low-voltage systems. The subject is approached from a systems point of view for low voltage applications, emphasizing the system interaction effects and the means that can be used to minimize this interaction. A detailed example is included to illustrate the use of the guidelines, which are applicable for a high percentage of low-voltage applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-tasking machine and process control for digital drives utilized in textile, fiber and film applications
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1991 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The benefits of using multitasking operating systems in textile applications are examined. The extrusion process is used to explore the demands placed on the system level controller, the digital drives, and the control engineer. The difficulties encountered with conventional control are discussed. The operation of an integrated multitasking controller is described, and the benefits of the approach are summarized. It is concluded that successful implementation of multitasking system controllers eases the burden placed on the control engineer by allowing the process problem to be addressed in manageable parts (tasks), and the unique software structure and high-level languages permit higher levels of flexibility and total integration in the process environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wiring and grounding to prevent power quality problems with industrial equipment
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1991 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: Actual case histories where inadequate wiring or grounding on low voltage (less than 600 V) industrial power distribution systems caused equipment operational problems and/or failures are examined, and the solution to each of these problems is discussed. The cases concern a malfunctioning peanut sorter, equipment damage at a wrecker service, personal computer malfunction at a city hall, disruption of a microprocessor-controlled quilting machine by an air compressor and electronic scale malfunction. Some of the case histories involve relatively rare grounding problems while others pertain to very common problems. Several of the most common wiring and grounding shortcomings found in low-voltage industrial power distribution systems are identified. Proper wiring and grounding techniques for equipment with electronic controls and application of these techniques in industrial facilities are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of control and information technology in the textile manufacturing environment
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1991 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: Innovations in control and information technologies that can provide a more highly integrated manufacturing environment capable of responding to marketplace demands are described. Specific trends in programming, man-machine interface devices, input/output control, and communications technologies are described and related to the textile manufacturing environment. Some of the trade-offs between system costs and benefits are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1991 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: It is shown that the advent of the microprocessor has had a significant impact on the latest generation of adjustable speed DC drives. The basic drive architecture is reviewed, and the extended functions offered by the standard microprocessor-controlled DC drive are discussed. Some of the most commonly used control functions are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of different power systems neutral grounding techniques: fact and fiction
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1991 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The characteristics of different power systems grounding techniques as currently applied, and misapplied, within industry today are examined: The concept of a grounding system is reviewed. Safety, National Electric Code requirements, and operational considerations, such as continuity of service, are investigated. Examples of proper applications within various industries are given. Selection criteria are included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementing an effective utility testing process: a keystone for successful energy management
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1991 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: Ongoing testing of selected pieces of power house utility equipment is described. This utility testing process (UTP) is a combined plant, central engineering, and consultant effort to capitalize on energy reduction efforts already completed and to provide a basis for obtaining the best possible level of performance. UTP objectives, fundamentals of operation for compressed air, chiller, and boiler systems, and maintenance considerations are covered. Details presented include the basic measurement approach, a layman's guide to available test equipment, techniques to employ, pitfalls to avoid, and evaluation of claims made by vendors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power factor improvement for nonlinear loads
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1991 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: Power factor correction through the application of capacitors to electrical systems is addressed, with particular reference to avoiding problems in systems where large nonlinear loads producing harmonic distortion are present. Power factor is reviewed, and a method for designing a power factor correction is presented. The approach has been successfully applied to industrial power distribution systems ranging in size from 550 to 10000 kVA. Four case studies, illustrating different aspects of the approach are presented. In all instances power factor was improved by reduction of both reactive and harmonic current loads on the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
